questions.q: A poison stops a cell's mitochondria working. What will the cell run short of?
A gland cell makes large amounts of protein. Which organelle would it have lots of?
Which statement about the cell wall and cell membrane is correct?
a: The wall gives structure; the membrane controls what enters and leaves
The membrane gives structure; the wall controls what enters and leaves
Both control what enters and leaves the cell
Animal cells have a wall but no membrane

questions.q: Chloroplasts and mitochondria are both linked to energy. What's the difference?
a: Chloroplasts absorb light for photosynthesis; mitochondria release energy by respiration
Chloroplasts release energy by respiration; mitochondria absorb light for photosynthesis
Both absorb light for photosynthesis, but only chloroplasts contain chlorophyll
Both release energy by respiration, but only mitochondria are found in animals

questions.q: Which of these is NOT an organelle?
questions.x: Cell sap is the liquid stored inside the vacuole, not a structure.

questions.q: Which organelle contains the instructions for making the cell's proteins?
questions.x: The nucleus holds the DNA (the instructions); the ribosomes do the actual making.

questions.q: Plant cells respire, so they have mitochondria as well as chloroplasts.
A cell has a nucleus, mitochondria, a cell wall and a vacuole but no chloroplasts. What is it most likely to be?
questions.x: Cell wall + vacuole = plant; no chloroplasts = underground.

questions.q: A cell has a nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, ribosomes and a cell membrane, and nothing else. What is it?
How many of these are found ONLY in plant cells: chloroplast, vacuole, cell wall, ribosome, mitochondrion?
Which of these is NOT found in a bacterium?
Which list contains ONLY unicellular organisms?
Bacteria are prokaryotic. Yeast cells have a nucleus, so yeast is...
All unicellular organisms are prokaryotic.
questions.x: Yeast, amoeba and euglena have a nucleus, so they're eukaryotic.

questions.q: Euglena has chloroplasts but an amoeba doesn't. What can euglena do that an amoeba can't?
Why must a specimen be cut very thin?
a: So light can pass through it
So it fits under the objective lens
So the stain doesn't run off

questions.q: In what order does light travel through the microscope?
a: Mirror → specimen → objective lens → eyepiece lens
Eyepiece lens → objective lens → specimen → mirror
Mirror → eyepiece lens → objective lens → specimen
Specimen → mirror → objective lens → eyepiece lens

questions.q: You've found the cells but they're slightly blurry. What do you adjust?
An image is very large but blurry. It has...
The view is completely dark. Which part is most likely set up wrongly?
Which two cells are both adapted to have a large surface area?
a: Red blood cell and root hair cell

questions.q: Root hair cells have many mitochondria. What is the energy used for?
a: Moving mineral ions into the cell
Moving the root hairs through soil

questions.q: Why are palisade cells tall and thin?
a: So lots can be packed together in the leaf
To give a large surface area for absorbing water
To reach the light at the top of the plant
To carry water up the stem

questions.q: Why do red blood cells have no nucleus?
Why does an egg cell have lots of cytoplasm with fat stores?
a: Energy to move along the oviduct
A store of food to attract sperm

questions.q: Ciliated epithelial cells have many mitochondria. Why?
a: Energy for the cilia to move
Energy to carry oxygen to the lungs
Energy to make the mucus sticky

questions.q: Apart from the airways, where are ciliated cells found, and what do they move there?
a: The oviducts; they move the egg
The blood vessels; they move blood

questions.q: Which adaptation is matched to the WRONG cell?
Which two cells both rely on many mitochondria to release energy for movement?
a: Red blood cell and nerve cell
Root hair cell and red blood cell

questions.q: What do the spongy outer layer of an egg cell and the tail of a sperm cell have in common?
a: Both are adaptations that help fertilisation
Both release energy for the cell to move
Both contain the DNA passed to the embryo
Both are made of tiny hairs called cilia

questions.q: Compared with eukaryotic cells, prokaryotic cells are...
a: Smaller and less complex, with no nucleus
Larger and more complex, with a nucleus
The same size but with no DNA

questions.q: Ice, water and steam are the same substance. Which has the lowest density, and why?
a: Steam: its particles are furthest apart
Ice: its particles are in a regular pattern
Water: its particles are close but random
Steam: its particles are the smallest
questions.x: The particles are the same size in every state; only the spacing changes.

questions.q: Which property do liquids and gases share?
a: They can flow and fill the shape of a container
They have a fixed volume that can't be changed
They can both be squashed into a smaller space
They both have a high density compared to solids

questions.q: Which property do solids and liquids share?
A syringe of air can be squashed but a syringe of water can't. Why?
a: Air particles are far apart; water particles are close
Water particles are heavier than air particles
Air particles are smaller than water particles
Water particles are fixed in a regular pattern

questions.q: Particles in a gas are bigger than particles in a liquid.
questions.x: Same particles; they're just further apart.

questions.q: Particles in a solid don't move at all.
questions.x: They vibrate around a fixed position.

questions.q: Which two changes of state need heat energy to be put IN?
When a solid melts, what happens to the particles?
a: They gain energy and overcome the forces of attraction
They get bigger and push each other further apart
They lose energy, slow down and spread out
They break apart into smaller and smaller particles

questions.q: Water droplets form on the outside of a cold can of drink. Where does the water come from?
a: Water vapour in the air condensing on the can
Drink seeping out through tiny holes in the can
Drink evaporating through the metal of the can
Ice inside the can melting through the metal

questions.q: Wet washing dries on a line on a cool day. Which change of state is this?
questions.x: Boiling needs the liquid to reach 100 °C; evaporation happens at the surface at any temperature.

questions.q: Dissolving and melting are the same thing.
questions.x: Melting needs heat (solid → liquid). Dissolving is solid particles spreading between liquid particles.

questions.q: When a liquid is cooled, its particles...
a: Lose energy, and the forces of attraction get stronger
Get smaller, so they can fit closer together
Stop moving completely and line up in rows
Gain energy, and the forces of attraction get weaker

questions.q: Which of these is a pure substance?
Sugar is stirred into hot water and disappears. Sugar is the ___ and water is the ___.
10 g of salt dissolves in 100 g of water. What is the mass of the solution?
questions.x: The salt particles are still there, just spread between the water particles.

questions.q: Salt dissolves in water but not in oil. What does this show?
a: Oil is a solute, not a solvent

questions.q: Salt water is an impure substance because...
a: It contains more than one substance
It contains salt, which is harmful
It is a liquid, not a solid
It can be separated by filtering

questions.q: Which of these is NOT an example of diffusion?
a: Water droplets forming on a cold window
The smell of cooking spreading through a house
A drop of ink spreading through still water
A tea bag colouring hot water

questions.q: In which states of matter can diffusion happen?
A purple crystal is left in still water. A day later the water is evenly purple. Why?
a: Its particles diffused until evenly spread
The crystal melted and spread through the water
The water evaporated and left the colour behind
The crystal's particles grew to fill the water

questions.q: Diffusion is faster in a gas than in a liquid. Why?
a: Gas particles move faster with more space
Gas particles are much smaller than liquid ones
Liquid particles don't move unless stirred
Gases are denser, so particles push harder

questions.q: To separate a mixture of sand and salt, what is the right order?
a: Add water, filter, then evaporate the filtrate
Filter, add water, then evaporate the residue
Evaporate, add water, then filter the solution
Add water, evaporate, then filter the crystals

questions.q: Which technique turns sea water into drinkable water?
questions.x: Evaporation keeps the salt but loses the water into the air.

questions.q: Which technique keeps the dissolved salt but lets the water escape into the air?
Which technique separates two liquids with different boiling points?
Why can't filtration separate salt from salt water?
a: Dissolved salt passes through the filter paper
Salt is insoluble, so it can't be filtered
Salt water is too thick to pass through paper
The salt water would dissolve the filter paper

questions.q: In chromatography, why must the solvent start BELOW the pencil line?
a: So the dyes don't wash into the solvent
So the paper doesn't get wet too quickly
So the pencil line doesn't run upwards
So the solvent front is easier to see

questions.q: Root hair cells do NOT have the part labelled ?. Why?
a: They need room for more mitochondria
They don't need to make glucose

questions.q: What type of cell is this, and why?
a: Prokaryotic: it has a cell wall

questions.q: The part labelled ? is packed with mitochondria. Why?
a: To store food for the embryo
To make the tail move by contracting

questions.q: What does the part labelled ? contain that helps it get into the egg?
a: Enzymes to digest the egg membrane
Fat stores to feed the embryo
Cilia to push it towards the egg

questions.q: What does the part labelled ? do?
a: Insulates the cell to speed up impulses
Connects the cell to other nerve cells
Releases energy to send the impulse
Stores the cell's DNA along the fibre

questions.q: Why does this cell have the branched endings labelled ??
a: To connect with other nerve cells
To increase surface area for absorbing oxygen
To anchor the cell in place

questions.q: What does the outer layer labelled ? do?
a: Protects the cell and attracts sperm
Stores fat to feed the growing embryo
Digests the tail of the sperm cell

questions.q: This cell's shape is a biconcave disc. What does that shape do?
a: Increases surface area to volume ratio
Makes space in the middle for a nucleus
Lets it swim through the blood plasma
Stops oxygen escaping once it's absorbed

questions.q: The particles in this state...
a: Move at random speeds in random directions

questions.q: Which properties does this state have?
a: Fixed volume, no fixed shape, can flow
Fixed shape, fixed volume, can't flow
No fixed volume, can be compressed
Fixed shape, no fixed volume, can flow

questions.q: Diffusion has stopped here. Why?
questions.x: The particles are still moving, but there's no longer an overall movement in one direction.

questions.q: After dissolving, where has the solute gone?
a: Its particles are between the solvent particles
Its particles have been destroyed by the water
Its particles have turned into a gas and left
Its particles have sunk to the bottom unseen

questions.q: Each particle here is made of two different atoms, yet this is a PURE substance. Why?
a: Every particle is the same (a compound)
It's a gas, so it can't be a mixture
The particles are spread out evenly

questions.q: Ink X is a mixture of which inks?
Why is the start line labelled ? drawn in pencil, not pen?
a: Pencil won't dissolve in the solvent
Pencil is easier to rub out if wrong
Pen would soak in and tear the paper
Pencil shows up better when wet
questions.x: Ink from a pen would dissolve and separate too, mixing up the results.

questions.q: What happens inside the part labelled ??
a: Water vapour cools and condenses into liquid
The salt water is heated until it boils
The salt is collected as the water leaves
The water is filtered to remove the salt

Filtrate: the insoluble solid left in the filter paper
